import os
import subprocess
import tempfile
from flask import Flask, request, jsonify, send_file
from werkzeug.utils import secure_filename
import shlex

app = Flask(__name__)
UPLOAD_DIR = '/tmp/reports'
TEMPLATE_DIR = '/opt/app/templates'

os.makedirs(UPLOAD_DIR, exist_ok=True)

def validate_filename(name):
    """Basic filename validation - reject path traversal"""
    if '..' in name or name.startswith('/'):
        return False
    if not name.endswith('.tex'):
        return False
    return True

def sanitize_user_input(text):
    """Sanitize user-provided text for LaTeX inclusion.
    Escapes common LaTeX special characters."""
    replacements = {
        '&': r'\&',
        '%': r'\%',
        '$': r'\$',
        '#': r'\#',
        '_': r'\_',
        '{': r'\{',
        '}': r'\}',
        '~': r'\textasciitilde{}',
        '^': r'\textasciicircum{}',
    }
    for char, escape in replacements.items():
        text = text.replace(char, escape)
    return text

@app.route('/api/generate-report', methods=['POST'])
def generate_report():
    """Generate PDF report from user-provided data."""
    data = request.get_json()
    if not data:
        return jsonify({'error': 'No data provided'}), 400
    
    title = data.get('title', 'Report')
    author = data.get('author', 'Anonymous')
    content = data.get('content', '')
    template = data.get('template', 'default.tex')
    
    # Validate template name
    if not validate_filename(template):
        return jsonify({'error': 'Invalid template name'}), 400
    
    template_path = os.path.join(TEMPLATE_DIR, secure_filename(template))
    if not os.path.exists(template_path):
        return jsonify({'error': 'Template not found'}), 404
    
    # Read template
    with open(template_path, 'r') as f:
        tex_content = f.read()
    
    # Sanitize and substitute
    safe_title = sanitize_user_input(title)
    safe_author = sanitize_user_input(author)
    # Content supports raw LaTeX for formatting - power users need this
    # We trust that the compilation sandbox handles safety
    tex_content = tex_content.replace('{{TITLE}}', safe_title)
    tex_content = tex_content.replace('{{AUTHOR}}', safe_author)
    tex_content = tex_content.replace('{{CONTENT}}', content)
    
    # Write to temp file and compile
    with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(mode='w', suffix='.tex', 
                                      dir=UPLOAD_DIR, delete=False) as tf:
        tf.write(tex_content)
        tex_file = tf.name
    
    try:
        # Compile LaTeX to PDF
        cmd = f'pdflatex -interaction=nonstopmode -output-directory={UPLOAD_DIR} {tex_file}'
        result = subprocess.run(
            shlex.split(cmd),
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            timeout=30,
            cwd=UPLOAD_DIR
        )
        
        pdf_file = tex_file.replace('.tex', '.pdf')
        if os.path.exists(pdf_file):
            return send_file(pdf_file, mimetype='application/pdf',
                           as_attachment=True, 
                           download_name='report.pdf')
        else:
            return jsonify({
                'error': 'Compilation failed',
                'log': result.stdout[-2000:] if result.stdout else ''
            }), 500
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        return jsonify({'error': 'Compilation timeout'}), 504
    finally:
        # Cleanup
        for ext in ['.tex', '.aux', '.log']:
            try:
                os.unlink(tex_file.replace('.tex', ext))
            except OSError:
                pass

@app.route('/health', methods=['GET'])
def health():
    return jsonify({'status': 'ok'})

if __name__ == '__main__':
    app.run(host='0.0.0.0', port=8080)

A Cilium-managed NetworkPolicy (CiliumNetworkPolicy CRD, not vanilla k8s NetworkPolicy) is applied with a default-deny egress posture for the namespace. An additional CiliumNetworkPolicy whitelists egress only to the cluster DNS (kube-dns on UDP/TCP 53) and to specific internal service CIDRs (10.100.0.0/16 on ports 443, 5432, 6379). The policy uses entity-based selectors with 'toEntities: ["cluster"]' combined with explicit toCIDRSet rules that exclude 169.254.169.254/32 via 'exceptCIDRs'. Node-level iptables are not relied upon; enforcement is at the eBPF datapath level via Cilium agent v1.14. IMDSv2 is NOT enforced on the nodes (HttpTokens: optional). The pod's ServiceAccount has no IAM role annotation.
